annotations.finding: Registered at YRGGBS00_SOURCE.txt:235 as substitution exit 'UXR2' (XREF2 field substitution). Body at lines 1024-1041. annotations.finding: UNESCO FMAVCT contains ONLY ALLOCTYPE_9='KBFC' (consumption) entries -- NO 'KBFB' (budget) entries. This means the AVC pool depth is computed by the FM-AVC engine at runtime as revenue (from FMIFIIT WRTTP=66) MINUS consumption (from FMAVCT KBFC). There is no static pool record.

SAPDBSDF is SAP-owned. A TIME_OUT at SAPDBSDF:1983 PUT_BSIS does NOT indicate a defect in the LDB or in SAP indexing. It reflects caller-side WP-time consumption during the GET bsis iteration. In INC-000006906 the actual clock was consumed by four MODE 'E' CALL TRANSACTION statements in YTBAE002 (FB08/F-04/FBRA) that opened SAPGUI on slow-WAN BDC errors. When investigating a TIME_OUT named against SAPDBSDF, ALWAYS look at what the caller does between successive GET events, not at the LDB SELECT itself.

Internal form of SAPDBSDF that fetches open GL items (BSIS) into the logical-database buffer. Line 1983 of SAPDBSDF is the failing SELECT. When caller program does not supply selective HKONT + BUDAT predicates, scan degrades and dialog dispatcher aborts with TIME_OUT.

SAP-standard row-delivery callback. A TIME_OUT blamed on PUT_BSIS:1983 means the work-process elapsed its rdisp/max_wprun_time cap while waiting in the caller's GET handler. The caller's shape (filter predicates) is only one axis of cost; the caller's GET-body work (BDC calls, FM calls, nested SELECTs) is an equal-or-larger axis. For INC-000006906 the latter dominates: GR_SAKNR_OI was non-empty (13 BSIS rows on 0001194424 live) but MODE 'E' BDC calls to FB08/F-04/FBRA in the GET loop consumed the clock.
